hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find France on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find France on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: France about 643,801 square kilometres; Morocco about 446,550 square kilometres; Trinidad and Tobago about 5,128 square kilometres; Saint Vincent and the Grenadines about 389 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with France?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture France on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the France article.

questions.proof: Metropolitan France is bordered (clockwise from the North) by Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Andorra, and Spain.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of France?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Franks” part of the France article.

questions.proof: The modern name "France" comes from the name of the Capetian Kings of France around Paris.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Paris?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of France is Paris.
